facts.text: A safety case consists of claims, reasoning and evidence within a stated context and set of assumptions; a collection of test reports alone is not a safety case.
facts.quote: A safety case is claims plus reasoning plus evidence within a stated context and set of assumptions, not a pile of test reports.

facts.text: Goal Structuring Notation depicts top-level goals framed by context, decomposed through strategies into sub-claims, and supported by solutions representing evidence. The cited references are Kelly (1998) and GSN Community Standard version 3, SCSC-141C (2021).
facts.quote: Goal Structuring Notation (Kelly, 1998; GSN Community Standard version 3, SCSC-141C, 2021) depicts top-level goals framed by context, decomposed through strategies into sub-claims and finally supported by solutions (evidence)

facts.text: Claims-Arguments-Evidence, associated with Bloomfield and Netkachova (2014), is the main alternative notation to Goal Structuring Notation.
facts.quote: Claims-Arguments-Evidence (Bloomfield and Netkachova, 2014) is the main alternative notation [129].

facts.text: ISO/IEC/IEEE 15026-2:2022 standardizes the assurance case.
facts.quote: ISO/IEC/IEEE 15026-2:2022 standardizes the assurance case

facts.text: OMG SACM provides a metamodel for assurance cases.
facts.quote: OMG SACM provides a metamodel

facts.text: Def Stan 00-56 Issue 7 requires safety cases for UK defence systems.
facts.quote: Def Stan 00-56 Issue 7 requires safety cases for UK defence systems

facts.text: UL 4600, third edition (2023), is the autonomous-products safety-case standard.
facts.quote: UL 4600 (3rd edition, 2023) is the autonomous-products safety-case standard

facts.text: ISO 26262-2:2018 requires a safety case for road vehicles; this is on-road evidence.
facts.quote: ISO 26262-2:2018 requires a safety case for road vehicles **(on-road evidence)**

facts.text: Nuclear regulation uses staged preliminary, interim and operational safety cases.
facts.quote: nuclear regulation uses staged preliminary, interim and operational safety cases

facts.text: Confidence arguments, associated with Hawkins and colleagues (2011), address confidence in a safety argument.
facts.quote: Confidence in the argument is handled by confidence arguments (Hawkins and colleagues, 2011)

facts.text: Eliminative argumentation with explicit defeaters, associated with Goodenough, Weinstock and Klein (2015), addresses confidence in a safety argument.
facts.quote: eliminative argumentation with explicit defeaters (Goodenough, Weinstock and Klein, 2015)

facts.text: The Assurance 2.0 manifesto by Bloomfield and Rushby (2020) addresses confidence in safety arguments.
facts.quote: the Assurance 2.0 manifesto (Bloomfield and Rushby, 2020)

facts.text: The taxonomy of fallacies in safety arguments by Greenwell and colleagues (2006) addresses confidence in safety arguments.
facts.quote: the taxonomy of fallacies in safety arguments (Greenwell and colleagues, 2006)

entities.name: taxonomy of fallacies in safety arguments

facts.text: Rinehart, Knight and Rowanhill's NASA reports (2015 and 2017) reviewed more than 50 sources and interviewed nearly a dozen practitioners to organize seven claimed benefits of assurance cases with evidence and counter-evidence for each.
facts.quote: Rinehart, Knight and Rowanhill's NASA reports (2015; 2017) reviewed more than 50 sources and interviewed "nearly a dozen" practitioners, organizing seven claimed benefits of assurance cases with the evidence and counter-evidence for each

facts.text: The efficacy evidence reviewed in Rinehart, Knight and Rowanhill's NASA reports (2015 and 2017) is mainly case studies.
facts.quote: the efficacy evidence is mainly case studies [23, 24].

facts.text: The Nimrod Review by Haddon-Cave (2009) shows that a safety case can become paperwork that nobody challenges.
facts.quote: The Nimrod Review (Haddon-Cave, 2009) shows that a safety case can become paperwork that nobody challenges

facts.text: Leveson (2011) and Graydon (2020) criticize confirmation bias and treating the graphical argument as the safety case instead of challenging the underlying evidence.
facts.quote: Leveson (2011) and Graydon (2020) are critical of confirmation bias and of treating the graphical argument as the safety case rather than challenging the underlying evidence

facts.text: A safety-argument diagram can become an impressive-looking justification for an unsupported premise.
facts.quote: A diagram can become an impressive-looking justification for an unsupported premise.

facts.text: Direct comparative evidence that Goal Structuring Notation or any notation improves heavy-machinery safety outcomes was not found.
facts.quote: Direct comparative evidence that GSN or any notation improves heavy-machinery safety outcomes was not found.

facts.text: Safety-case notation is documented practice without outcome evidence; its value for the heavy-off-road-machine virtual-validation programme is structuring what the evidence must show.
facts.quote: Verdict: documented practice without outcome evidence; its value for this programme is structuring what the evidence must show.

facts.text: A candidate top-level claim for the virtual-validation programme is that, within machine configuration M, operating envelope E and safety-function scope F, the defined virtual-test process produces evidence credible enough to support engineering decision D with explicitly bounded residual uncertainty.
facts.quote: Within machine configuration M, operating envelope E and safety-function scope F, the defined virtual-test process produces evidence credible enough to support engineering decision D with explicitly bounded residual uncertainty.

facts.text: The proposed decomposition of the virtual-validation safety claim synthesizes NASA model-credibility practice, ASME VVUQ, Goal Structuring Notation and integrated test-and-evaluation practice.
facts.quote: It is a synthesis of NASA model-credibility practice, ASME VVUQ, GSN and integrated test-and-evaluation practice.

facts.text: To support the proposed claim that intended use and scope are valid, the virtual-validation roadmap should create a context-of-use statement and evidence covering hazards, exclusions and applicable standards.
facts.quote: | Intended use and scope are valid | Context-of-use statement; hazards; exclusions; applicable standards |

facts.text: To support the proposed claim that computational implementation is correct enough, the virtual-validation roadmap should create code and tool verification evidence, regression tests and solver checks.
facts.quote: | The computational implementation is correct enough | Code and tool verification, regression tests, solver checks |

facts.text: To support the proposed claim that simulation represents the real system sufficiently for its intended use, the virtual-validation roadmap should create correlation and validation evidence against independent test or field data.
facts.quote: | The simulation represents the real system sufficiently for the intended use | Correlation and validation against independent test or field data |

facts.text: To support the proposed claim that inputs are trustworthy, the virtual-validation roadmap should create data-lineage, calibration, measurement-uncertainty and data-quality records.
facts.quote: | Inputs are trustworthy | Data lineage, calibration, measurement uncertainty, data-quality records |

facts.text: To support the proposed claim that scenarios adequately represent the safety question, the virtual-validation roadmap should create hazard-to-scenario traceability and a coverage rationale.
facts.quote: | Scenarios adequately represent the safety question | Hazard-to-scenario traceability and coverage rationale |

facts.text: To support the proposed claim that uncertainty is understood, the virtual-validation roadmap should document parameter, model-form and measurement uncertainty and perform sensitivity analysis.
facts.quote: | Uncertainty is understood | Parameter, model-form and measurement uncertainty; sensitivity analysis |

facts.text: To support the proposed claim that the toolchain is repeatable, the virtual-validation roadmap should create version control, a configuration baseline and a reproducibility record.
facts.quote: | The toolchain is repeatable | Version control, configuration baseline, reproducibility record |

facts.text: To support the proposed claim that evidence stays inside the validated domain, the virtual-validation roadmap should create an applicability envelope and extrapolation rules.
facts.quote: | Evidence stays inside the validated domain | Applicability envelope and extrapolation rules |

facts.text: To support the proposed claim that residual gaps are acceptable, the virtual-validation roadmap should create an open-evidence and deviation log with signed disposition.
facts.quote: | Residual gaps are acceptable | Open-evidence and deviation log with signed disposition |

facts.text: To support the proposed claim that conclusions follow from the evidence, the virtual-validation roadmap should provide independent technical and safety review and a claim-to-evidence trace.
facts.quote: | Conclusions follow from the evidence | Independent technical and safety review; claim-to-evidence trace |

facts.text: Several frameworks for the credibility of virtual testing now exist and are converging.
facts.quote: **Credibility of virtual testing.** Several frameworks now exist and are converging.
